Manually assembled for iteration-2's flat eval/configuration layout, using the standard metadata/runs/result/expectations/run_summary fields. No automatic aggregator was used.

Rubric source: .opencode/skills/web-deploy-security/evals/evals.json, nine expectations per eval. eval_metadata.json assertions copy those exact expectations and prompts. Eval names retain the established directory names because the source eval entries contain no name field.
Aggregate with_skill: 18 passed, 0 failed, 18 total (100%). Aggregate without_skill: 14 passed, 4 failed, 18 total (7/9 = 77.77777777777778%). Difference: 2/9 = 22.22222222222222 percentage points.

Only two scenarios, with a single run per scenario/configuration in each iteration. runs_per_configuration=1 denotes that per-eval repeat count, not two independent repeats. The zero sample standard deviations describe equal scores across two different scenarios, not repeatability or statistical certainty.

Resumed agents retain previous-run context. The exposure with-skill agent reported accidentally seeing two expectation lines from eval 1 (report.md:41). This is not a rigorous blinded evaluation and does not isolate the causal effect of the skill.

No full tool transcripts are available. Process claims are report assertions only; the reported expectation exposure is recorded as a limitation, not independently reconstructed. Unknown durations, tokens, models, tool-call counts and execution errors are omitted, not zero-filled. Timestamp records benchmark preparation in UTC, not executor timing.

Iteration 1 used seven expectations per eval: with_skill 14/14 (100%), without_skill 13/14 (92.85714285714286%). Iteration 2 on those same first seven expectations is also with_skill 14/14 and without_skill 13/14. Shared-rubric scores are unchanged.

The four added expectation instances contribute with_skill 4/4 and without_skill 1/4. Do not interpret iteration 2's raw 77.78% baseline versus iteration 1's 92.86% as performance regression: the denominator and checks expanded. Iteration-1 files were not regraded or modified.

Qualitative with-skill improvements are observable: eval 1 no longer assigns FastAPI/protocol/CSRF intent without evidence; eval 2 splits the failed FILE-01 serving outcome from its unknown configuration cause. Both full matrices and pending lists reconcile to the checklist.

Remaining scored defects are confined to the without-skill reports: eval 1's unsupported TCP label, both reports' absent counted full-family coverage, and eval 2's missing port/file inventory and developed coverage structure. Both configurations otherwise preserve appropriate publication decisions and supplied-evidence limits.
